chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Dawood, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the words of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family): 'When the man commits adultery, the spirit of faith separates from him.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is like the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
and when they spend, they do so not out of extravagance nor stinginess
Then he (peace be upon him) said: 'That is more explicit than this. That is the word of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
and He strengthened them with a Spirit from Him
That is the one which separates from him.
ai.seo_question: What is the Quranic basis for the 'spirit of faith' separating upon adultery?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the hadith regarding the departure of the 'spirit of faith' (ruh al-iman) upon committing adultery by drawing a parallel to Quranic terminology. He initially references Surah Al-Furqan 25:67 to establish the concept of spiritual impurity, but clarifies that the more precise allusion is to Surah Al-Anfal 8:12, where the 'Spirit' that strengthens the believers is identified as the very essence of faith that departs upon this major sin. This interpretation highlights the ontological link between divine grace and the permanence of faith in the believer's heart.
